text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Kabariti says King Hussein trying to get Hamas leaders Sheikh Ahmed Yassin and Moussa Abu Marzouq released. Confirms reports that Jordan looking at possibility of Marzouq being transferred from U.S. to Jordan.
- Sudanese Islamist leader Turabi thanks Jordanian people and the Moslem Brotherhood for their support for Sudan.
- Crown Prince Hassan, visiting France for talks with French President Chirac, says East Jerusalem is Arab and Israel's annexation is null and void.
- Qatari newspaper says Kuwait is considering releasing Jordanian prisoners in Kuwaiti jails.
- Minister for Municipal Affairs Tbeishat says plans for February 27 municipal elections proceeding smoothly.
- Central Bank governor Ziyad Fariz says International Monetary Fund's extra $47 million made available to Jordan will be offered in three tranches, starting this year.
- Nine nationalist and centrist parties try to merge ahead of this year's parliamentary elections, sources say.
- Crown Prince Hassan and Chirac discuss peace process and building security in the Middle East.
- Kabariti discusses coordinated policy with Egyptian ambassador for Arab-Israeli final settlement talks.
- Doctors drop plans for protest over bonus pay; engineers stand firm.
- Jordan seized 100 kg (220 pounds) of hashish, one kg (2.2 pounds) of heroin, 254 drug capsules and 55,000 forged U.S. dollars in January.
- Stock exchange hits highest levels since 1995.
- Unified Company for Organising Land Transport reports 1.2 million dinar ($1.69 million) profit in 1996, plans to distribute profit worth 11 percent of capital to its shareholders.
- Jordan in efforts to secure release of Hamas leaders Sheikh Yassin and Abu Marzouq.
